beats.act: cold open
beats.narration_text: Aloha. This is Liam, in for Bear, with lecture one of Computational Skepticism for AI. A sepsis model ran in hundreds of hospitals and passed every test. Then someone checked it against the patients. What went wrong? Nothing, by the builders' measures. It missed two of every three. The gap between those sentences is the course.

beats.act: ACT I: TWO FAILURES THAT PASSED
beats.narration_text: The first failure. An external team checked a widely deployed sepsis model against twenty-seven thousand, six hundred ninety-seven hospitalized patients. The model missed roughly two of every three who went on to develop sepsis.

shot.visual_intent: Isotype: three patient figures in a row; two grey out on 'two of every three'; counter '27,697 patients' lands at the top; the ghosted figures carry the accent.

graphic.note: FACTCHECK SEED rows 2–3. Isotype encodes the 67% miss rate as a count, not a percentage bar.

beats.act: ACT I: TWO FAILURES THAT PASSED
beats.narration_text: The other side: alerts on eighteen percent of all hospitalized patients, the large majority of whom were never septic. The model's AUC — its discrimination ability — was point six three. Barely above guessing.

beats.act: ACT II: DESCARTES — WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE?
beats.narration_text: Act two. Descartes: what would have to be true?

beats.act: ACT II: DESCARTES — WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE?
beats.narration_text: Descartes: before you trust a claim, ask what would have to be true for it to be wrong. Applied to the sepsis model: the training data underweighted these cases. The input features missed the relevant signal. The deployment context differed from the validation context. Three checkable engineering questions.

shot.visual_intent: Three checkbox rows land in sequence on their spoken conditions: 'training data underweighted these cases' · 'input features missed the signal' · 'deployment context ≠ validation context'; each checkbox is open on arrival and ticks terracotta on 'three checkable engineering questions'.

beats.act: ACT II: DESCARTES — WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE?
beats.narration_text: August first, 2012. Knight deploys to eight servers. Seven receive the update. One does not. A reused flag wakes Power Peg — dead code from 2003. Forty-five minutes: four million executions across one hundred and fifty-four stocks, roughly four hundred and forty million dollars. The deployment said green.

beats.act: ACT III: HUME — THE TURKEY WITH A SPREADSHEET
beats.narration_text: Hume's move: the limit of induction. A turkey is fed every morning for a thousand days. Each feeding increases its confidence the next day will also bring food. By day nine hundred and ninety-nine, very high probability of a meal. Day one thousand: the axe.

shot.visual_intent: A line chart: x-axis 'Day 1 → Day 1000', y-axis 'Confidence in tomorrow's meal'; the line climbs steadily for 999 ticks; on day 1000 the line drops to zero; a terracotta axe mark at day 1000.

show.event: Line reaches near-maximum at day 999 on 'nine hundred ninety-nine'
Line drops to zero; axe mark on 'the axe'

graphic.mechanic: A line chart: x-axis 'Day 1 → Day 1000', y-axis 'Confidence in tomorrow's meal'; the line climbs steadily for 999 ticks; on day 1000 the line drops to zero; a terracotta axe mark at day 1000.
graphic.note: FACTCHECK SEED row 12. Schematic; x-axis goes to 1000.

beats.act: ACT III: HUME — THE TURKEY WITH A SPREADSHEET
beats.narration_text: The turkey knew the correlation. It did not know the mechanism. An AI trained on a hospital's historical cases has done exactly the same thing. When the patient population shifts, a new pathogen arrives, demographics change — the model cannot notice. It was not built to notice.

shot.visual_intent: Two boxes: 'What the model knows' (correlation: pattern held for N cases) and 'What the model cannot see' (three arrows incoming: population shift · new pathogen · changed demographics). The three arrows pulse terracotta on 'cannot notice'.

show.event: 'What the model cannot see' box draws

graphic.mechanic: Two boxes: 'What the model knows' (correlation: pattern held for N cases) and 'What the model cannot see' (three arrows incoming: population shift · new pathogen · changed demographics). The three arrows pulse terracotta on 'cannot notice'.
graphic.note: FACTCHECK SEED row 23. The mechanism-blindness of induction applied to AI deployment.

beats.act: ACT III: HUME — THE TURKEY WITH A SPREADSHEET
beats.narration_text: The model's confidence is a property of the model. Not of the world. The world is under no obligation to match the model's expectations.

beats.act: ACT IV: POPPER — TRY TO BREAK IT
beats.narration_text: Act four. Popper: try to break it.
beats.motion_claim: Act label lands first; the headline springs in on the second beat — two staged reveals, then a hard cut.

beats.act: ACT IV: POPPER — TRY TO BREAK IT
beats.narration_text: Popper's asymmetry. No finite count of white swans proves all swans are white. One black swan ends the claim. Confirming instances pile up without certainty. A single falsifying instance provides it. You cannot prove a model works in all cases. You can prove it fails in this one.

shot.visual_intent: Left side: white swan icons accumulate in a stack, counter climbing on 'pile up'; label 'confirming instances: no certainty'; right side: one black swan icon appears alone on 'one black swan'; label 'one falsifying instance: certainty'; terracotta bracket on the right side on 'provides it'.

show.event: Left stack begins accumulating white swans
Counter climbs; 'no certainty' label lands on 'pile up'
Single black swan appears on the right on 'One black swan'

graphic.mechanic: Left side: white swan icons accumulate in a stack, counter climbing on 'pile up'; label 'confirming instances: no certainty'; right side: one black swan icon appears alone on 'one black swan'; label 'one falsifying instance: certainty'; terracotta bracket on the right side on 'provides it'.
graphic.note: FACTCHECK SEED row 23. The asymmetry is the move; the swans are the vehicle.

beats.act: ACT IV: POPPER — TRY TO BREAK IT
beats.narration_text: The move converts rhetoric into engineering. 'The system is robust' becomes a specific threshold. 'The model performs well' becomes a precision and recall floor. 'The migration succeeded' becomes a latency cap. Rhetorical claims are compatible with any outcome. Engineering claims specify the conditions under which they would be false.

shot.visual_intent: Two columns: 'Rhetorical' (the system is robust · the model performs well · the migration succeeded) vs 'Engineering threshold' (precision ≥ X, recall ≥ Y · latency ≤ Z ms · specific falsification condition). Rows land on spoken items; caption '*illustrative thresholds'.

graphic.mechanic: Two columns: 'Rhetorical' (the system is robust · the model performs well · the migration succeeded) vs 'Engineering threshold' (precision ≥ X, recall ≥ Y · latency ≤ Z ms · specific falsification condition). Rows land on spoken items; caption '*illustrative thresholds'.
graphic.note: FACTCHECK SEED row 19. Illustrative thresholds captioned as such — no real values claimed.

beats.act: ACT IV: POPPER — TRY TO BREAK IT
beats.narration_text: This is the test the sepsis model never got. Internal validation: white swans accumulated — the vendor counted every correct prediction. External validation: the black-swan test, an outside team designed to break it. On twenty-seven thousand patients, it failed. Unrefuted is not validated. From the dashboard, they look identical.

shot.visual_intent: Left panel 'Internal validation': white swan icons accumulate; 'vendor counts correct predictions'. Right panel 'External validation': one black swan icon; 'outside team · 27,697 patients · failed'. Footer in terracotta: 'Unrefuted ≠ Validated'.

Right: black swan + '27,697 patients' on 'outside team'

beats.act: ACT V: THE CAVE, AND THE FLUENCY TRAP
beats.narration_text: The Cave move is three questions on every output. What is the artifact? What is the world? What is the relationship between them? The triage score was the artifact. The clot was the world. The relationship was correlation, not mechanism.

beats.act: ACT V: THE CAVE, AND THE FLUENCY TRAP
beats.narration_text: COMPAS predicts recidivism. The artifact: a number. The world: a person's future conduct. The relationship: mediated by arrest data shaped by who gets policed. The model learned the pattern of policing, not the pattern of behavior. Artifact, world, relationship — three different things.

shot.visual_intent: Three-row anatomy table: ARTIFACT (a number) · WORLD (a person's future conduct) · RELATIONSHIP (arrest data shaped by who gets policed → pattern of policing, not behavior). Rows land on spoken items; RELATIONSHIP row takes the terracotta accent.

beats.act: ACT V: THE CAVE, AND THE FLUENCY TRAP
beats.narration_text: The fluency trap runs in two moves. Polished output boosts your confidence in the answer — that part is expected. The trap is the second arrow: that confidence then boosts your trust in your own evaluation. Fluency is an evaluation booster. It does not distinguish correct from incorrect.

shot.visual_intent: A two-step arrow diagram: 'Polished output' → 'Confidence in the answer' (grey arrow, expected); then a second arrow 'Confidence in the answer' → 'Trust in your own evaluation' (terracotta, the trap); the second arrow takes the accent on 'second arrow'.

'Trust in your own evaluation' box with accent

graphic.note: FACTCHECK SEED row 22. The two-arrow structure is the whole point; one draw per arrow.

beats.act: ACT V: THE CAVE, AND THE FLUENCY TRAP
beats.narration_text: Form and content are independent. An AI produces maximally fluent prose about things it has no basis to say. A sentence looks like knowledge because well-formed sentences usually are knowledge. That heuristic fails here. Fluency and correctness are two different sliders, moving independently.

shot.visual_intent: Two horizontal sliders side by side: 'Fluency' and 'Correctness'. The Fluency slider moves to the right on 'maximally fluent'; the Correctness slider stays at the left; they decouple on 'independently'.

graphic.note: FACTCHECK SEED row 22. The slider diagram encodes decoupling without numerical values.

beats.act: ACT V: THE CAVE, AND THE FLUENCY TRAP
beats.narration_text: Do not let fluency do epistemic work. Specify the wrong answer before you read. Then ask whether the output matches your specification.

beats.act: ACT VI: CHEAP TO PRODUCE, EXPENSIVE TO VERIFY
beats.narration_text: Act six. Cheap to produce, expensive to verify.

beats.act: ACT VI: CHEAP TO PRODUCE, EXPENSIVE TO VERIFY
beats.narration_text: The classical asymmetry: factoring is hard, multiplying to check is easy. AI deployment inverts it. Producing the output: milliseconds, fractions of a cent. Verifying it: a clinician's twenty minutes, an hour of senior labor. The effort has moved from producing to checking.

shot.visual_intent: Two schematic bar pairs; left pair 'Classical': 'factor' bar tall, 'check' bar short; right pair 'AI deployment': 'produce' bar short (terracotta accent), 'verify' bar tall; a flip arrow between the pairs on 'inverts'; no numerals; caption 'schematic'.

graphic.note: FACTCHECK SEED row 20. Schematic only — no numerical ratios.

beats.act: ACT VI: CHEAP TO PRODUCE, EXPENSIVE TO VERIFY
beats.narration_text: If you do not budget for verification, you will not get verification. Automating the checking is just another model, one layer up, with the same problem.

beats.act: ACT VII: FIVE WAYS TO WATCH
beats.narration_text: Act seven. Five ways to watch.
beats.motion_claim: Act label lands first; the headline springs in on the second beat — two staged reveals, then a hard cut.

beats.act: ACT VII: FIVE WAYS TO WATCH
beats.narration_text: Five supervisory capacities. Plausibility auditing: does this output make sense given what I know? Problem formulation: is the model answering the question that matters? Tool orchestration: is AI the right tool here? Interpretive judgment: what does this number mean in this domain? Executive integration: where does the buck stop?

beats.narration_text: Problem formulation is the load-bearing one. The triage model answered: what is the statistical category of this presentation? The clinical question was: does this patient have a life-threatening condition? Different questions. The first was answered well. The second was never asked. Most AI failures are failures of problem formulation.

beats.act: ACT VII: FIVE WAYS TO WATCH
beats.narration_text: Individual skepticism is fragile. Institutional skepticism writes the moves into the workflow — the falsification condition on the checklist, the distribution-shift test in the handoff protocol. The five capacities become a design question: where, by whom, seeing what. That architecture determines whether the patient is safe.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Valid by the builders' measures; wrong at the bedside. Doubt: what would have to be true for this to be wrong?
